technical.summary: Mixed momentum signals with short-term bullish technicals (RSI, Stoch, Supertrend) offset by weak intermediate trend structure and price below key moving averages; moderate confluence but lacks strong directional conviction.

fundamental.summary: MMM shows no insider buying conviction, no institutional accumulation signal, zero government contracts, no lobbying activity, minimal retail interest, and earnings in 14 days creating elevated event risk.

sentiment.summary: No actionable congressional signal; mixed market sentiment (slight bearish bias 35% vs bullish 33%) with greed reading (57) provides neutral backdrop; insufficient data for conviction.

risk.summary: Severe macro headwinds: inverted yield curve signals recession risk, VIX at crisis levels (170.6) indicates extreme market stress, CPI event in 1 day adds near-term volatility, and earnings in 14 days create binary event risk for industrials.

debate.key_bull_argument: Short-term momentum (RSI rising, stochastic bullish cross, supertrend bullish) with price near support (76.57) offers tactical entry for mean-reversion trade if macro volatility stabilizes.
debate.key_bear_argument: Severe macro headwinds (inverted yield curve, VIX crisis at 170.6, CPI event in 1 day, earnings in 14 days), price below all key moving averages, MACD negative, and zero fundamental conviction create unacceptable risk/reward for swing entry.

decision.entry_rationale: Short-term momentum technicals (RSI rising, stochastic bullish cross, supertrend) offer tactical appeal at support, but macro environment and earnings proximity create unacceptable risk/reward asymmetry for new swing entry.
decision.primary_risk: VIX crisis (170.6), inverted yield curve, CPI event in 1 day, and earnings in 14 days create compounding volatility and binary event risk that overwhelms short-term momentum signals.
decision.agent_agreement: strong — all agents aligned on bear case dominance
decision.portfolio_note: Already holding MMM position with 10 existing Industrials positions (19.6% sector concentration); adding exposure increases concentration risk during macro stress without fundamental conviction.
